sections.heading: Visa
sections.body:
Visa
As of March 1, 2025, Iraq is no longer issuing visas on arrival. All travellers must now apply for an eVisa prior to their arrival in Iraq. If you are from one of the below countries, your eVisa will be issued within 24 hours of your application. We can also apply on your behalf for a lower fee than the official government rate.
The list of the countries:

Permanent members of the Security Council:
(UK, USA, France, Russia, China).

EU Countries:
(Germany, Italy, Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Denmark, Ireland, Gibraltar, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Austria, Finland, Estonia, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Croatia).

Countries with strong economic ties with Iraq:
(Australia, Canada, South Korea, Japan) Also (New Zealand, Switzerland, Norway and Hong Kong).

Gulf Council of Cooperation Countries:
(Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Oman).

sections.heading: e-Visa
sections.body:
e-Visa
Iraq's eVisa Portal started on the 15th of February 2024. This will make the visa application process as easy and hassle-free as possible.

All citizens of other nationalities don't need to visit an Iraqi embassy or Iraqi consulate anymore! All you need is a valid passport and personal photo of yourself and finalise your trip details with us. We will take care of everything else for you.

sections.body:
Electricity
230 V, 50 Hz

sections.heading: Passport
sections.body:
Passport
You will need your passport in all Iraqi checkpoints and hotels. Make sure you have at least six months valid on your passport on your arrival date, and an empty page in your passport for the Iraqi visa sticker, otherwise you might have some issues at the border.
Make sure you have no stamp on your passport from regions that have no recognition from Iraq. The region is: (the Israel entity).

sections.heading: Airport
sections.body:
Airport
There are five international airports in Iraq.
The main one is Baghdad International Airport, located 16km away from downtown Baghdad. It is the country's largest air hub, and home base for the national airline (Iraqi Airways) where passengers can take its flights within Iraq such as Baghdad - Erbil or Basra, and also travel to some regional destinations.
Connections are available to destinations worldwide via other regional airlines such as Turkish Airlines, Qatar Airways, Emirates, Royal Jordanian and many others. Our transfer has been pre-arranged within the package. No need to buy a mobile SIM card from the airport, as our logistical team will help you do this in the city.
Most of our itineraries start in Baghdad and end in Erbil or Basra. Just double check with us before booking your flight.

sections.heading: Currency and Gold Carrying Limit
sections.body:
Currency and Gold Carrying Limit
Each traveller is allowed to carry up to $5,000 or its equivalent in gold (130g) without declaration. For amounts exceeding $5,000 up to $10,000, declaration at customs is required. Carrying more than $10,000 in currency or gold is not permitted. Please note that this limit is calculated per person travelling.

sections.heading: Money
sections.body:
Money
You will find it tough to find many stores that will accept cards. Your best option would be bringing all the cash you will need for your trip with you beforehand. ATMs are available but not common in Iraq, and occasionally the servers will go down, so it won't be possible to withdraw any money. Bringing USD will not be a big problem as it is also accepted and exchanged. The most preferable notes are (100$ and 50$) issued in the year of 2006 and after.

sections.heading: Currency Information
sections.body:
Currency Information
Iraqi Dinar (IQD; symbol ID). In use notes are in denominations of IQD (50,000 - 25,000 - 10,000 - 5,000 - 1,000 - 500 - 250).
1$ = 1,320 IQD is the official rate. But usually, 1$ = 1,500 IQD in daily use in the market.

sections.heading: Tips
sections.body:
It is up to you to ask for a hand to help you out. If someone is asking to help you and you do not need it, just say no thank you!
In case you accepted the help then your tips in hotels or airports should not be more than 5,000 IQD.
It is always welcomed to tip more if you are happy or liked the service of the person.
To tip our staff, just use the same tradition that you do in your country. Iraq is your home too!

sections.heading: Clothing
sections.body:
Clothing
It is always wise to dress respectfully. You should not stress too much about what to wear, but as a general rule of thumb, especially for women, you should try and cover as much of your shoulders and knees as you can. Long pants and loose-fitting t-shirts. Ideally, skirts should cover your ankles but covering just your knees would be fine too.
In holy shrines, men are not allowed to wear shorts and women should wear scarves and Abaya. Our female team will help you wear the suitable dressing — do not worry at all, you are all welcomed to visit. Follow the weather forecast to know more about what you should wear and bring with you.
